topic: Honest minimax risk and confidence-length frontier for noninvertible threshold modified-treatment policies under polynomial generalized-propensity thinning. On the fixed finite-stratum Holder model, prove the exact natural-course-plus-Dirac decomposition, let h solve n h^(2 beta+1)(delta+h)^kappa asymptotic to one, and establish the sharp rate n^(-1/2)+delta^(kappa+1)h^beta with its regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes. Construct a total-Gram-stabilized local-polynomial atom estimator and bias-aware uniformly honest interval attaining the rate for every declared threshold sequence, and prove matching same-class global-shift and localized-Bernoulli lower bounds. Use the official lmtp threshold-policy workflow as consumer and do not smooth or replace the target. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The target equals an observable natural-course mean plus q_x(delta)mu_x(delta), with q_x(delta) asymptotic to delta^(kappa+1). Local information is n h(delta+h)^kappa, so Holder bias-variance balance gives the stated scale. For beta=kappa=1, pi(a)=2a yields h=(n delta)^(-1/3), KL of order n delta h^3, target separation delta^2h, and transition delta=n^(-1/10). Searches found threshold policies explicitly excluded from published LMTP EIF theory although the package accepts user policies. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform realized-design total-Gram lemma, under only two-sided polynomial density bounds, controlling exact local-polynomial l1/l2 weights and the singular-Gram fallback probability tightly enough for honest O(r_n) expected length over all deterministic delta sequences. EARLY KILL TEST: In the one-cell beta=kappa=1 class with arbitrary measurable density c_-a<=pi(a)<=c_+a, prove those weight and bad-event bounds and a finite-sample honest interval of length O(n^-1/2+delta^2h); pivot or stop if propensity smoothness is unavoidable.

open_problems.open_problem: For the official lower-threshold modified treatment policy d_delta(a)=max(a,delta), what is the sharp minimax risk frontier over finite-stratum Holder outcome regressions when the generalized propensity is only two-sided comparable to a^kappa and delta=delta_n follows an arbitrary deterministic sequence?

source_refs.claim: LMTP identification is general, but continuous-exposure EIF, efficiency, and root-n estimator theory assumes piecewise smooth invertibility, which clamping violates.
source_refs.author: Ivan Diaz, Nicholas Williams, Katherine L. Hoffman, Edward J. Schenck
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The LMTP tutorial flags threshold interventions as non-pathwise-differentiable and outside the piecewise-smooth-invertible continuous-exposure theory.
source_refs.author: Katherine L. Hoffman, Diego Salazar-Barreto, Nicholas T. Williams, Kara E. Rudolph, Ivan Diaz

source_refs.claim: The lmtp software paper documents the package workflow for user-specified modified treatment policies, creating a consumer-facing boundary beyond the published threshold theory.
source_refs.author: Nicholas T. Williams, Ivan Diaz

source_refs.claim: Pointwise regression under a regularly varying degenerate design has a thinning-dependent minimax rate, but the target is an unweighted fixed point value rather than an atom-weighted causal mean at a moving threshold.
source_refs.author: Stephane Gaiffas

source_refs.excerpt: No claims are made about efficient influence functions ... or continuous-treatment LMTPs in this version.
The open object is the converse: complete the Le Cam / Assouad handle on W_n^lb
the per-observation chi-square is ... bounded by C m_n q_n h_n^2

open_problems.why_unsolved: The LMTP density-ratio EIF argument changes variables through locally invertible policy branches; d_delta collapses [0,delta] onto one point, so the pushforward has a Dirac component and no ordinary post-policy density ratio. Gaiffas treats an unweighted fixed point value, not the composite of a regular natural-course mean and q_x(delta)mu_x(delta) at a moving point. The prior weak-overlap proposal also leaves its shell-sensitive Le Cam/Assouad converse open, while the accepted policy-regret construction controls a localized divergence for a different estimand. A solution must simultaneously prove the mixed-measure decomposition, exploit local information n h(delta+h)^kappa, and construct same-class alternatives whose atom-weighted separation matches the upper rate in every regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact observable natural-course-plus-q_x(delta)mu_x(delta) decomposition and matching minimax upper and lower risk bounds, uniform over deterministic delta_n, with h solving n h^(2 beta+1)(delta+h)^kappa asymptotic to one and an explicit regular/critical/atom-dominated/fixed-threshold phase diagram.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its arc from feasible natural-value-dependent interventions to identification and estimator theory, then make the exact excluded clamp policy the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Static continuous-dose interventions strain relevance and positivity -> LMTPs encode feasible modifications of natural treatment -> existing continuous-exposure theory requires piecewise smooth invertibility -> clamping creates an atom and requires nonregular minimax theory

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the regular-variation bias-information balance and localized two-point lower-bound construction for pointwise regression under a vanishing random-design density.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The atom term requires mu(delta_n) at a moving point with local design mass of order h(delta+h)^kappa; the LMTP multiplier changes the target separation but not the local testing geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the doubly robust pseudo-outcome followed by local-polynomial smoothing, including its nuisance-product remainder and asymptotic-normality proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It turns a continuous-treatment causal problem into local regression at a dose, the same statistical subproblem as estimating the threshold atom, but without thinning or atom-mass attenuation.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a total-Gram-stabilized local-polynomial atom estimator support a bias-aware confidence interval that is uniformly honest and has minimax-order expected length for every deterministic threshold sequence under only two-sided polynomial design-density bounds?

source_refs.claim: Bias-aware local-polynomial intervals are nearly minimax and honest, including at boundaries, but the design is treated as fixed or subject to regular design-sequence conditions.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: A conditioned-on-design local-polynomial estimator with Gram stabilization adapts to regularly varying degenerate random design, paying an unavoidable logarithmic adaptation cost.
source_refs.author: Stephane Gaiffas

source_refs.excerpt: that counting obstruction does not rule out ridge, pseudoinverse, rare-cell, or other stabilized procedures
specify a Poisson-calibrated interval and formulate its conditional coverage target
Add a concrete two-point or Poisson-experiment lower-bound route for the honest-diameter question

open_problems.why_unsolved: Armstrong-Kolesar calibrate worst-case smoothing bias after fixing the regression design, so their expected-length proof does not absorb a singular random local Gram event. Gaiffas conditions on a regularly varying design and controls an eigenvalue good event, but does not give exact l1/l2 intercept-weight bounds plus a fallback probability uniformly over every measurable density satisfying c_-a^kappa<=pi(a)<=c_+a^kappa. The banked dose-response proof assumed fixed positivity, and the initiation-time reviewers separately identified Poisson calibration and honest-diameter lower bounds as missing. The first step that must change is the realized-design argument: normalize by total local mass, prove deterministic weight geometry, and integrate the fallback event before applying a bias-aware critical value.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Finite-sample realized-design l1/l2 weight and singular-Gram tail bounds, followed by a computable interval with uniform coverage at least 1-alpha and worst-case expected length O(n^(-1/2)+delta^(kappa+1)h^beta), using an explicit Poisson or exact calibration when the effective local count stays bounded.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from honest coverage through explicit worst-case bias to optimal expected length, while foregrounding the new random-design bad-Gram obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conventional local-polynomial intervals ignore smoothing bias -> honesty requires worst-case bias calibration -> expected length is the minimax criterion -> vanishing random design requires total-Gram stabilization to retain both guarantees

method_exemplars.technique: Port the conditioned-on-design local-polynomial Gram matrix, eigenvalue good event, fallback construction, and regular-variation probability bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest proof-level treatment of local polynomials where random-design density vanishes at the target, exactly where the threshold atom is estimated.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the worst-case Holder bias calculation, bias-aware critical value, and expected-length efficiency comparison based on exact local-polynomial weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once conditional weight norms and fallback probability are controlled, this supplies the interval construction and length benchmark required by the resolution.

open_problems.open_problem: Is uniformly honest adaptation to unknown Holder smoothness beta and unknown thinning exponent kappa possible for the deterministic threshold-LMTP mean, and if not, what is the exact unavoidable inflation in confidence length?

source_refs.claim: For pointwise regression under a regularly varying degenerate design, adaptation to unknown signal smoothness and design behavior incurs an unavoidable logarithmic loss.
source_refs.author: Stephane Gaiffas

source_refs.claim: Optimal honest confidence length for a linear functional is governed by a between-class modulus, and data-dependent tightening cannot generally preserve coverage over the full smoothness class.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing adaptation results concern an unweighted point value, whereas the difficult LMTP component is q(delta)mu(delta), with q(delta) both revealing the thinning exponent and possibly shrinking fast enough for the regular n^(-1/2) term to dominate. That attenuation changes the between-class modulus and may remove or relocate the price of learning kappa at critical threshold sequences. Neither the degenerate-design Lepski lower bound nor the fixed-design modulus theory covers this composite causal functional, and the targeted search found no adaptive honest result for the unsmoothed clamp target.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive interval with uniform coverage and a class-indexed expected-length oracle inequality over declared (beta,kappa) ranges, or a constrained-risk/modulus lower bound giving the exact logarithmic or polynomial adaptation penalty and the threshold sequences on which it is unavoidable.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its setup of locally scarce information, unknown design degeneration, and a precise payment-for-adaptation question, then explain how the atom multiplier changes the benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Local information depends on an unknown vanishing design -> bandwidth must adapt to design and regression smoothness -> point estimation pays a logarithmic price -> the LMTP atom multiplier may change where that price is necessary

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the Lepski selector based on empirical local mass and Gram conditioning, together with the constrained-risk lower-bound argument for the payment for adaptation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It jointly treats unknown smoothness and unknown local design degeneration at the point underlying the threshold atom.

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered moduli between convex smoothness classes to turn adaptation limits into finite-sample and asymptotic expected-length lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired resolution is specifically an honest confidence-length frontier, the performance criterion controlled by their modulus method.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax-optimal simultaneous confidence band over a continuum of thresholds for the unsmoothed deterministic clamp LMTP when the threshold index crosses regular, critical, and atom-dominated thinning regimes?

source_refs.claim: This paper gives efficient estimation and simultaneous bands for a threshold-response curve, but redraws sub-threshold doses from a support-restricted law rather than applying d_delta(A)=max(A,delta).
source_refs.author: Lars van der Laan, Wenbo Zhang, Peter B. Gilbert

source_refs.claim: Simultaneous inference is developed for contrasts of LMTP outcome trajectories, while threshold interventions are explicitly excluded as non-pathwise-differentiable.
source_refs.author: Anja Shahu, Weijie Xia, Ying Wei, Daniel Malinsky

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Biometrics threshold-response band avoids point evaluation by replacing sub-threshold doses with a draw from the above-threshold distribution, so it cannot be reinterpreted as inference for the official deterministic clamp. Smooth-LMTP Gaussian process theory explicitly excludes threshold policies. Under clamping, the atom location and mass both vary with delta and the normalization changes at the bias-variance transition, so a single root-n Donsker band is invalid. Searches found bands for stochastic region-average targets and smooth LMTP trajectories, but not for this target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of the threshold-indexed process and a uniformly honest simultaneous band with matching minimax sup-width, or an impossibility theorem showing that adaptation across the regime transition requires a specified logarithmic penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its policy-facing threshold-curve motivation and simultaneous-inference formulation while sharply distinguishing its stochastic intervention from the deterministic clamp.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Scientific decisions vary with a threshold -> a threshold-indexed causal curve is more useful than one cutoff -> simultaneous inference is needed for comparisons -> the deterministic clamp needs a nonregular band rather than a region-average band

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its threshold-index empirical-process organization and simultaneous critical-value construction, replacing the regular EIF curve by stabilized atom estimators with threshold-dependent normalization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest causal threshold paper with simultaneous bands, and its region-average target makes the proof step that fails for clamping explicit.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bias-aware local-polynomial critical values and modulus calculations pointwise, then couple them over the threshold index.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nonregular component is a continuum of weighted boundary point evaluations whose widths must account for Holder bias.

open_problems.open_problem: For longitudinal LMTPs that clamp a continuous exposure at one or more visits, what minimax rate and honest limit theory arise from the recursively generated mixed continuous-atomic treatment histories?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives sequential-regression identification and SDR/TMLE theory for longitudinal LMTPs, with continuous-exposure optimality theory restricted to piecewise smooth invertible policies.
source_refs.author: Ivan Diaz, Nicholas Williams, Katherine L. Hoffman, Edward J. Schenck
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper extends smooth-LMTP inference to outcome trajectories and rates of change but explicitly excludes threshold interventions as non-pathwise-differentiable.
source_refs.author: Anja Shahu, Weijie Xia, Ying Wei, Daniel Malinsky

open_problems.why_unsolved: The causal mean remains accessible through sequential regression, but published efficiency proofs represent every post-policy treatment law by an ordinary density ratio. A clamp at the first visit creates an atom inside later histories; later clamps split the law into multiple continuous and atomic components whose masses couple through the recursion. The first proof step to change is the density-ratio EIF recursion itself, replacing it by a mixed-measure decomposition and stagewise nonregular remainder analysis. Searches found longitudinal LMTP inference for smooth shifts and trajectories, but no deterministic clamping atoms or minimax phase diagram.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A recursive mixed-measure representation of the longitudinal target and an estimator with a proved joint limit law and matching minimax rate expressed through visit-specific thinning exponents, Holder smoothnesses, atom masses, and threshold sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its longitudinal progression from counterfactual policy definition to sequential identification to estimator theory, with deterministic atoms isolated as the missing regime.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Realistic interventions depend on each natural treatment value -> longitudinal LMTPs handle time-varying confounding by sequential regression -> smooth invertible policies admit SDR/TMLE inference -> repeated clamping creates mixed laws requiring a new nonregular recursion

method_exemplars.technique: Retain backward sequential-regression identification while replacing the change-of-variable density representation by a Lebesgue-plus-Dirac pushforward decomposition at each visit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its recursion identifies the same natural-value-dependent longitudinal target; the measure representation used for optimality and estimation is the step that fails.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the stacked longitudinal influence-function and simultaneous-contrast machinery after substituting stagewise stabilized atom estimators and non-root-n normalizations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest inference framework for multiple LMTP-indexed longitudinal outcomes and explicitly marks threshold policies as outside its scope.

literature_map:
Diaz, Williams, Hoffman and Schenck (JASA 2023; arXiv:2006.01366) identify longitudinal LMTPs and derive EIF/SDR/TMLE theory only under piecewise smooth invertibility for continuous exposure.
Hoffman et al. (Epidemiology 2024; arXiv:2304.09460) explicitly flag threshold interventions as non-pathwise-differentiable and outside that theory.
Williams and Diaz (Observational Studies 2023; doi:10.1353/obs.2023.0019) document the lmtp software workflow for user-defined policies, exposing a practice-theory boundary.
Shahu et al. (Statistics in Medicine 2026; arXiv:2508.11131) give simultaneous LMTP trajectory inference but explicitly exclude threshold interventions.
Haneuse and Rotnitzky (Statistics in Medicine 2013; doi:10.1002/sim.5907) introduced received-treatment modifications and the piecewise-invertible change-of-variables route.
van der Laan, Zhang and Gilbert (Biometrics 2023; arXiv:2107.11459) obtain efficient estimation and simultaneous bands for a stochastic support-restricted threshold-response target, not deterministic clamping.
McCoy et al. (arXiv:2302.07976) study data-adaptive exposure-region averages, avoiding the clamp's point mass by changing the estimand.
Kennedy et al. (JRSSB 2017; doi:10.1111/rssb.12212) give a doubly robust pseudo-outcome plus local-linear estimator for a continuous dose-response.
Colangelo and Lee (JBES 2026; arXiv:2004.03036) develop kernel-localized cross-fit DML under ordinary continuous-treatment overlap, not polynomial thinning.
Bonvini and Kennedy (arXiv:2207.11825) analyze local, global, and higher-order dose-response rates but not an atom-attenuated clamp functional or honest intervals.
Gaiffas (Mathematical Methods of Statistics 2005; arXiv:math/0410354) gives pointwise minimax rates under a regularly varying degenerate random design.
Gaiffas (ESAIM P&S 2007; arXiv:math/0503715) adds local-polynomial Gram stabilization and adaptive bandwidth selection with an unavoidable logarithmic loss.
Armstrong and Kolesar (Quantitative Economics 2020; arXiv:1606.01200) give bias-aware nearly minimax honest local-polynomial intervals for fixed-design regression.
The unoccupied intersection is the exact unsmoothed clamp LMTP, its natural-course-plus-Dirac geometry, polynomial thinning, moving thresholds, and honest minimax confidence length.
